preconditions: A functionally correct C-simulation baseline exists.
A real synthesis report provides latency, clock, loop, and resource evidence.
entries.action: Choose one measurable bottleneck and change only one optimization class before re-synthesizing.
entries.expected_signal: The limiting report metric improves and the effect is attributable to the selected action.
contraindications: Do not stack directives on an unverified baseline.
Remove or revise a directive that does not improve the limiting metric.

preconditions: The synthesis report shows achieved II above the target.
The blocker can be classified from timing, recurrence, memory-port, or interface evidence.
entries.action: Classify the II blocker first. If the exact array/recurrence/timing cause is absent, return the kernel unchanged; never add a standalone PIPELINE directive as an II fix.
entries.expected_signal: Achieved II moves toward target II without disproportionate worst-resource growth.
contraindications: Do not infer memory pressure from top interval alone.
Do not add another PIPELINE directive without matching the measured blocker.

preconditions: A specific loop or function scope controls throughput.
Loop structure and current achieved II are known.
entries.action: Apply PIPELINE to the throughput-controlling scope with a report-supported II target.
entries.expected_signal: Loop interval or function throughput improves while timing and resource capacity remain valid.
contraindications: Outer-loop pipelining may force inner-loop concurrency and expose memory-port pressure.
Do not add PIPELINE when the measured loop is already II=1 and latency is trip-count dominated.

preconditions: A statically bounded loop dominates latency.
The loop is already pipelined effectively or exposes independent iterations.
Resource headroom is available.
entries.action: Try one loop-local partial UNROLL with the smallest useful factor, then measure latency, clock, and worst-resource growth.
entries.expected_signal: Effective latency improves more than the worst proportional resource growth.
contraindications: Do not fully unroll a long or dynamically bounded loop.
Do not increase a factor after measured resource growth outweighed speedup.

preconditions: Synthesis identifies parallel accesses or a memory-port II lower bound on a named array.
The contended array dimension and required access factor are known.
entries.action: Apply ARRAY_PARTITION to the measured array and access dimension, using the minimum factor that can satisfy the required ports.
entries.expected_signal: The memory-port II lower bound falls and achieved II improves.
contraindications: Do not partition unrelated top-level arrays speculatively.
Do not combine ARRAY_PARTITION and ARRAY_RESHAPE on the same variable.
Over-partitioning can increase LUT, FF, and BRAM disproportionately.

preconditions: Adjacent elements are consumed together.
The limiting evidence is storage or interface word width rather than independent-bank access.
entries.action: Apply ARRAY_RESHAPE to the adjacent access dimension with a width/factor justified by the consumer lanes.
entries.expected_signal: Useful bandwidth per access increases without unnecessary bank replication.
contraindications: Do not use reshape for irregular or independent-bank access.
Do not combine ARRAY_RESHAPE and ARRAY_PARTITION on the same variable.

preconditions: The dominant computation is an associative reduction.
The operator, accumulator type, numerical behavior, and desired tree shape are explicit.
entries.action: For a statically bounded associative integer reduction, first try only a loop-local partial UNROLL factor=2; preserve the accumulator and numeric contract. Do not introduce a new tree architecture in this phase.
entries.expected_signal: The loop-carried accumulation path shortens and effective latency improves at acceptable area cost.
contraindications: Do not restructure non-associative floating-point operations without permission.
Unrolling without an accumulator policy can hide overflow and timing risk.

preconditions: The source has matrix-multiply-style nested loops.
Tile shape, layout, accumulator type, and local reuse are explicit.
entries.action: Preserve the existing GEMM architecture. If the source already has tiled/local reuse, try only one small loop-local UNROLL factor=2; add banking only for an exact measured port bottleneck. Do not introduce new tiles or buffers in this phase.
entries.expected_signal: External accesses per MAC fall and compute parallelism improves effective latency within resource limits.
contraindications: Do not copy template interfaces or fixed tile sizes into an existing kernel.
Do not partition tiles without a visible reuse and access-dimension argument.

preconditions: The source performs repeated neighborhood access over a 2D or 3D grid.
Window shape, boundary policy, and reuse distance are known.
entries.action: Preserve the existing stencil architecture and boundary behavior. First try only a small UNROLL factor=2 on a statically bounded filter loop; do not introduce a new line buffer in this phase.
entries.expected_signal: Memory traffic falls and the stencil loop sustains a lower interval.
contraindications: Do not change the boundary policy.
Do not apply both partition and reshape to the same line buffer.

preconditions: The kernel has clear producer, compute, and consumer stages.
Channel ownership and bounded producer/consumer behavior are explicit.
entries.action: Tune DATAFLOW only when a DATAFLOW region and explicit stage boundaries already exist. Do not introduce a new task graph in this phase; every change requires real CoSim.
entries.expected_signal: Stage execution overlaps and throughput approaches the slowest stage interval.
contraindications: Do not introduce DATAFLOW into shared mutable state or ambiguous stage ownership.
C simulation alone cannot prove bounded FIFO behavior or absence of RTL deadlock.

preconditions: Producer and consumer rates or burst sizes can differ.
The channel is an hls::stream or equivalent bounded FIFO.
entries.action: Set an evidence-based explicit channel depth and verify backpressure, stall behavior, and required CoSim.
entries.expected_signal: Required CoSim completes without deadlock while FIFO resources remain bounded.
contraindications: Do not use a very large depth to hide an architectural ordering bug.
Do not claim deadlock safety from C simulation.

preconditions: An outer loop is considered for pipelining.
Inner-loop access concurrency and memory ports can be inspected.
entries.action: Model the implied inner-loop concurrency before outer-loop PIPELINE; add banking only when the accessed dimension proves it.
entries.expected_signal: Outer-loop throughput improves without unresolved port conflicts or uncontrolled resource replication.
contraindications: Do not treat outer PIPELINE as a syntax-only change.
Do not guess partition dimension or factor.
